The Service Desk

Boards, tickets, notes, clocks and everything a technician does to a ticket, from the moment it lands to the moment it closes.

For technicians and service managersBoards and ticketsAbout 25 minutes
Boards

Boards and membership

TechniciansService managers

A board is one team's queue. You see a board's tickets only if you are its member, with one of three levels.

MembershipYou can
ReadSee the board and its tickets.
WorkAlso take, note, time, schedule and change tickets.
AdminAlso run the board's Setup: statuses, SLA, templates, notes, members, emails, auto-assign.
Service boardIncidents, requests, problems and events, with SLA clocks. The PMO Helpdesk is one.
Change boardChanges, with assessment, approval and scheduling. See the Change guide.
Project boardProject work with no SLA clocks. See the Projects guide.
Restricted boardOnly its members see it, and every read of its tickets is audited, a system administrator's included.

Everyday moves

  • Filter by board, status, owner, priority, type, source and words; save the view under a name for tomorrow.
  • Tick rows to change status, owner or board together, or attach them to a parent ticket.
  • Keys: j k move, x ticks, Enter opens, n new ticket, / search, Ctrl K jumps anywhere.
Tickets

Priority

Everyone

Priority is worked out from two plain questions, never typed.

Try it: how the two questions set the priority
Who is affected?
Is a patient waiting?
?
Answer both questions.
No patient waitingWaiting, with a workaroundCare stopped or unsafe
Just meP4P4P3
Ward or severalP4P3P2
Whole hospitalP3P2P1

Nobody types a priority. A catalogue item can carry a floor that lifts it, and work that touches care is never below P2.

Tickets

The SLA clocks

TechniciansService managers

Three clocks run on every service ticket, each against a target for its priority, on the board's working hours and holidays.

ClockStops when the ticket reachesPaused by a waiting status?
RespondIn Progress, Scheduled, Resolved (any status that counts as responded)Never: parking a ticket is not a response
Resolution planScheduled or ResolvedYes
ResolveResolvedYes
Try it: move a ticket and watch its clocks

Reading the chips on the board

ChipMeans
R ✓Respond met.
P 40mResolution plan due in 40 minutes.
S -2dResolve target passed by two days.
S pausedStopped while the ticket waits.

The starter targets are placeholders: P1 respond 15 minutes, plan 1 hour, resolve 4 hours; P4 respond 8 hours, plan 1 day, resolve 3 days. Each board's service manager sets its own on the SLA tab.

The cards

CardWhat you do there
TicketBoard, status, owner, company, contact, type and Subtype › Item, and the two priority questions.
TimeRecord time: start and end or hours, a deduction, the work role and type, the bill option and the charge method.
TasksA checklist; ticking records who and when. A template can add tasks.
ScheduleBook a visit for yourself or a colleague: status, where, lead, done, acknowledged.
FamilyAttach child tickets, or merge a duplicate into this one.
FilesPhotos and documents, checked for patient details before a requester sees them.
ConfigurationsThe machines the ticket is about, with a remote-control launch where set up.
KnowledgeArticles for this Subtype › Item first; link the one that helped.
FinanceBizBox records the ticket concerns.
ApprovalsAsk a person to approve before the work is done.
Tickets

Notes and emails

Technicians
Which kind of note should I write?
Pick the one that fits.
  • Standard notes are a board's canned replies. Each carries its flag, so a we have your request reply cannot land as internal by accident.
  • Emails never carry the summary or a note. They say something changed and link to PMC Requests.
  • Each board decides whether requesters and owners get emails, and in what words (Setup › the board › Emails).

Tickets

Files

Technicians

Attach a screenshot, a photo of the machine, a log or a document. Up to 10 MB each.

  • What is allowed is decided by the file's own bytes: images, PDF, text and logs, CSV, Office documents, email. Programs and scripts are refused.
  • Photos lose their location and camera details; screenshots lose their hidden text chunks. Nothing visible changes.
  • Every file is checked for patient details before a requester can see it: Pending, then Cleared or Withheld. A withheld file is served to nobody.

Tickets

Logging a ticket for someone

Technicians
  1. Press New ticket or n.
  2. Choose the board and the contact; the company follows the contact.
  3. Answer the two questions: the priority is worked out.
  4. Write the summary and what they told you. No patient details.
  5. Save. The requester sees it on PMC Requests like any other.
